news.title: Ireland-England U15 World Cup match abandoned following racism allegation
news.lede: THE REPUBLIC OF Ireland’s match with England at the U15 World Cup on Monday was abandoned following an allegation of racism. England walked off the pitch after an altercation between players from both sides in the final minute of the game in Azerbaijan. Ireland were leading 4-1 at the time. Match footage from DAZN shows an English player speaking to the referee and then approaching his coaching staff about the incident.

news.title: England Under-15s walk off pitch against Ireland in World Cup after racism allegation
news.lede: Match in new Fifa competition abandoned. England players refuse to resume match. England abandoned their Under-15 World Cup match against the Republic of Ireland on Monday after a player reported being subjected to a racist slur. Fifa confirmed it was investigating what happened in the final minute of the Group C fixture in Baku, Azerbaijan, when Ireland were leading 4-1.

news.title: FIFA issue statement as England walk off pitch at U15 World Cup after alleged racism
news.lede: FIFA are investigating an allegation of racist abuse by a Republic of Ireland player that led to the abandonment of England's Under-15 World Cup match. The incident took place during Monday's match in Azerbaijan, when an England player was seen approaching the touchline to inform his coaching staff of the alleged abuse, before the complaint was brought to the referee's attention. England's coaching staff then instructed their players to leave the pitch, with the Republic of Ireland leading 4-1 heading into the final minute of the match. FIFA have since confirmed they are investigating the incident and gathering reports to establish the circumstances surrounding the allegation.

news.title: Asian football endorses Infantino re-election as FIFA president
news.lede: The head of the Asian Football Confederation on Friday said the region supported Gianni Infantino's bid for re-election as FIFA president following weeks of fierce criticism of his aborted World Cup selloff plan. The 56-year-old Swiss was present at a Tokyo meeting of the AFC when president Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa gave his unequivocal backing. Sheikh Salman had previously condemned Infantino over his plan to open FIFA's premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors. Infantino has faced calls to quit and had lost the support of many associations in his bid to be re-elected to a fourth and final term.

news.title: FIFA U-17 World Cup Qatar 2026 tickets now on sale | Gulf Times
news.lede: General public tickets for the FIFA U-17 World Cup Qatar 2026 are now on sale at www.roadtoqatar.qa, as Qatar gets ready to welcome young generation for yet another spectacular edition of the prestigious competition. Taking place from November 19 to December 13, the FIFA U-17 World Cup Qatar 2026 will be held at the state-of-the-art Competition Complex at Aspire Zone, with 48 teams competing across 104 matches. The final will take place at Ahmad bin Ali Stadium. Fans can be part of the electrifying football festival-like atmosphere by purchasing a Day Pass, which will enable them to attend up to eight matches a day at Aspire Zone, as well as cultural and entertainment activities at the Fan Zone.

news.title: England U15s walk off pitch during World Cup match after racism allegation
news.lede: The Young Lions' fixture at the FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival was abandoned on Monday. Head coach Matt Thorpe withdrew his players in the final minute of the match following the incident. According to the Daily Mail, an England player claimed an opponent had made a racist comment towards them. It followed an altercation which saw the England youngster push a rival in the back.

news.title: FIFA U-17 World Cup Qatar 2026 trophy tour set to kick off at Doha Festival City on October 29 | Gulf Times
news.lede: Football enthusiasts and families across Qatar will have the opportunity to see the FIFA U-17 World Cup Qatar 2026 trophy, as the prestigious tournament trophy will make its way to key vibrant destinations nationwide ahead of the global showpiece. The trophy tour will take place at the following locations:Doha Festival City: Date: Thursday, October 29; Time: 6pm-10pmWest Walk: Date: Thursday, November 5: Time: 6pm-10pmMsheireb Downtown Doha: Date: Thursday, November 12. Each stop will feature engaging fan activities and photo opportunities with the official trophy, as Qatar once again prepares to host 48 international teams competing across 104 matches from November 19 to December 13. The FIFA U-17 World Cup Qatar 2026 is the second of five consecutive editions that Qatar will host through 2029.
